title: fix(docs): stop pricing the eager-closure ruling with a page count nothing derives, and teach the pin the hyphenated form
body:
Fixes #9004

The Docs Route Eager Closure section of `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` argued its structural-vs-byte-level ruling by pricing the alternative as a docs build of a stated size, and the eager-closure gate's own header mirrored the same sentence. Nothing derived either figure. Both sentences keep the cost argument and drop the cardinality; the pin that was supposed to catch this learns the hyphenated attributive, and the mirror site gets an assertion of its own.

Verified on `b7b24c5df`, with a freshly fetched `origin/main` (`2c878be17`) merged in first.

---

## The card's three questions, answered

### 1. Does the sentence keep a number at all? — ⛔ No, and neither copy does.

⭐ The claim is an **argument about cost**, not a reading of today's tree: a byte budget would have to build the whole collection, and that is true at any size. The cardinality is the only part of the sentence that can rot, and it carried no weight in the argument.

⭐ The decisive fact is local: the same section, six lines above the defect, already says «⛔ No page count here, deliberately» and names what the population is derived from — `apps/site/source.config.ts`'s collection directory and the gate's `gauge:` line. The page was contradicting itself inside one section. Stating a number against a named commit is the right remedy for a *past measurement worth keeping* (the four correct sentences on that page do exactly that), but this sentence has no measurement behind it to date — it is a hypothetical price, so there is nothing to name a commit for. ⛔ Inventing a replacement, live or dated, is the defect this family exists about.

Both sentences now say "every page of that collection", which is derived by the paragraph the reader is already in.

### 2. Do the two copies stay two? — ⭐ The sentences stay two; the figure goes to zero.

They are not two copies of a measurement that must be kept in sync — they are two audiences. The page argues the ruling for readers of the CI guide; the gate header argues it for whoever next maintains the script and wonders why it does not weigh bytes. Collapsing either into a pointer at the other would make one of them unreadable where it is read, and a cross-file pointer is its own maintenance burden. What must not be two is the **number**, and after this change neither site states one.

### 3. Does the noun pattern gain the hyphenated attributive? — ⭐ Yes, and the reason it was thought not to be safe does not survive reading the carriers.

The card and its triage both say the widening touches every carrier of objectui#7448's family, so no single pin may make it alone. ⭐ Read rather than described, that is **false**. The `\s+` shape is not shared: it is a `const population` defined **inside** the `describe` block of the ci-cd-pipeline pin, and the family's other two carriers each spell their own, differently:

| carrier | separator between numeral and noun | sees `N-page`? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the ci-cd-pipeline populations pin | `\s+` — whitespace only | ⛔ no (the gap this card is about) |
| the lint-workflow `object-ui/*` rule-count pin | a bounded any-character gap | ✓ already |
| the merge-queue subscribing-workflows pin | a bounded any-character gap | ✓ already |

⇒ this carrier was the **narrowest of the three**, not the shared one. Widening its separator to `[\s-]+` has a blast radius of one file, and the two carriers that were supposed to be endangered already accept the hyphenated form. All three were run, not assumed — verdicts below.

⚠️ And a second reading the claim comment asked for: a widened pattern does **not** reach the gate header or the pin's own docblock, because every assertion in that block is built from a named section of the docs page. That is why the gate header needed an assertion of its own rather than inheriting one.

---

## ⭐ Able to fail — both halves, red then green, restored by hash

**The doc half.** The separator was widened *before* the prose was touched, so the existing assertion could be seen failing on the untouched tree:

```
× states no docs-page population, and names what derives it instead
AssertionError: the Docs Route Eager Closure section states a docs-page population
again (found "556-page"). ...: expected '556-page' to be undefined
Tests  1 failed | 78 passed (79)
```

⇒ 1 failure, and exactly one: the other two `population()` call sites in the same block (the `skills` file count and the sweeper's page window) stayed green, so the widening reddens nothing else in this carrier. After the prose fix: `Tests 80 passed (80)`.

**The gate-header half.** The new assertion was ablated twice from the committed state, each run proving the mutation reached disk before the verdict was read, each restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ...` and checked by blob hash, not by exit code:

| mutation injected into the committed tree | verdict | what the assertion printed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| a spaced count put back in the gate header | `1 failed \| 79 passed (80)` | found `"181 pages"` |
| the hyphenated form put back in **both** repaired sites | `2 failed \| 78 passed (80)` | found `"556-page"`, twice |

Restore proof for both: `git diff HEAD` empty, and `git hash-object` on each touched path equal to its `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` blob. ⭐ The second row is the regression this card is actually about — before this PR neither site could have gone red on it.

---

## ⚠️ A second underived population in the same header, removed with it

The gate header carried **two**, not one. Besides the priced docs build it also charged an import to a stated page count — the same `181 docs pages` wording objectui#8629 removed from the docs page, which survived here because this file is outside `content/docs/**`. It is provably false: the collection holds **184** git-tracked `.md`/`.mdx` files on `2c878be17`, of which 144 are `.mdx`, which is what the gate's `gauge:` line reports (`gauge: 1381 modules crawled from 148 route roots (144 MDX)`).

⚠️ This is not scope creep bolted on: the new assertion **cannot be green with it present** — that is the first ablation row above, run against the real text. Guarding the mirror site at all required removing it, so it is removed, and said so here rather than slipped in.

---

## ⭐ The gap record was rewritten, ⛔ never swept

The pin's docblock quotes the figure in order to explain why the pin could not see it, and naming this card by number. ⛔ A sweep that greps the figure and removes every hit deletes the one artefact explaining the defect's own invisibility, so it was not treated as an occurrence. It changed only because this card's ruling on the pattern made it stale, and it was rewritten deliberately to record, in order: what the gap was, that it is now closed and by which card, ⛔ that the reason given for not closing it — the shared-pattern premise — does not survive reading the carriers, and what the widening still does not reach and therefore needed its own assertion.

⇒ the record still explains the defect; it now also explains the fix and the limit of the fix.

---

## Gates run, with their printed verdicts

| command | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| the three family carriers + the eager-closure gate's own test | `Test Files 4 passed (4)` · `Tests 129 passed (129)` |
| every other test that reads any touched file (11 files) | `Test Files 11 passed (11)` · `Tests 459 passed (459)` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅ No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` — 3 files changed, 0 published source, **no changeset owed, so none added** |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | `✅ No pending changeset names a file this change touches.` |
| `pnpm check:docs-route-closure` | exit 0 — all 13 registrar packages accounted for, ledger honest, `gauge: 1381 modules crawled from 148 route roots (144 MDX)` |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 7312 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0` |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | exit 0 — and the pin file is proven inside that program (`--listFiles` names it), so the green is a measurement, not an exclusion |
| `pnpm lint:root` (whole root population, 12s) | exit 0 — 32 pre-existing warnings, **0 errors** |

⛔ No assertion in the pin file was weakened, narrowed or deleted; the block goes from 79 to 80 tests.

---

## Found and ⛔ not done here

Two more stated populations of the same class, outside this card's sites, filed bare for triage:

- **#9116** — `registerCatalogBlocks.ts`'s header states `all 181 docs pages`, `556/556 static pages` and `440 thumbnail frames` as live facts with no commit named. ⭐ It is the likely **provenance** of the figure this PR removed: a Next prerender total, transplanted into a claim about a collection it was never a count of.
- **#9117** — the strict-authoring-face argument prices its corpus as `no document among the 556`, in a source header and again in the test docblock that depends on it. The load-bearing claim there is «zero», not «556».
